sports.h3: Verstappen wins wet Singapore Sprint and takes GP pole
sports.summary: Max Verstappen won the first ever Sprint at Marina Bay after George Russell crashed out of the lead, then beat Charles Leclerc to pole for today's Grand Prix.
body: Max Verstappen finally broke his Singapore duck on Saturday, winning a rain-hit Sprint that started late because of standing water at Turns 2 and 3. Russell beat him into the first corner on the damp track but went off on the second lap, later blaming more battery deployment than he expected. Verstappen then controlled the shortened 20-lap race to finish 2.591 seconds clear of Lewis Hamilton, with Leclerc third.

It was his first Sprint win of the season and his first victory of any kind at Marina Bay. Attrition was heavy: eight of the 22 starters were out by lap 15, Lance Stroll and Sergio Perez collided and the two McLarens tangled on the final lap. Kimi Antonelli, Liam Lawson, Oliver Bearman, Nico Hulkenberg and Lando Norris completed the points.

Under the lights in the evening, Verstappen added his first career Singapore Grand Prix pole with a 1m 31.373s set on his first run, just 0.054s ahead of Leclerc. Hamilton was quickest in Q1 and Q2 but could not improve on his final lap and starts third, ahead of Antonelli and Norris. The race starts at 14:00 Dutch time.

sports.h3: Russell takes grid drop as Antonelli stretches title lead
sports.summary: Mercedes' George Russell starts the Singapore GP from the back half of the grid after an engine change, while team mate Kimi Antonelli now leads the title race by 89 points.
body: George Russell's bad Saturday did not end with his Sprint crash. The Mercedes driver took sixth in qualifying knowing he faces a hefty grid penalty for fitting a new engine, so every driver classified behind him gains a place. He also reported smelling fire in the car during Q1.

Antonelli's fourth place in the Sprint stretched his championship advantage over Russell to 89 points. McLaren's weekend went the other way: Oscar Piastri recovered from his last-lap collision with Norris to qualify seventh, while Red Bull's Isack Hadjar retired from the Sprint and could not set a representative lap in qualifying.

sports.h3: Zheng becomes first Chinese finalist in Beijing
sports.summary: Wild card Zheng Qinwen beat Elise Mertens 7-5, 6-2 to set up a China Open final against Mirra Andreeva today.
body: Zheng Qinwen ended Elise Mertens' giant-killing run on Saturday night, winning eight of the last ten games to take the semifinal 7-5, 6-2 in 92 minutes. The Olympic champion is the first Chinese player to reach the final of her home WTA 1000 event in Beijing and is now chasing her first title at that level.

Her opponent is fourth seed Mirra Andreeva, who beat Nikola Bartunkova 6-2, 6-2 and has not dropped a set all week. The pair have met once before, in the 2024 Beijing quarterfinals, when Zheng came from a set down to win. A strong result would push Zheng back toward the top 30 after a resurgent two months.

sports.h3: Moustached Alcaraz starts Shanghai bid in 66 minutes
sports.summary: Carlos Alcaraz beat Juan Manuel Cerundolo 6-3, 6-3 to stretch his winning streak to seven matches and set up a meeting with Zizou Bergs.
body: Fresh from defending his Tokyo title, Carlos Alcaraz needed just 66 minutes to open his Shanghai campaign. He hit 24 winners and won 13 of 20 trips to the net, saying the fast court suited an attacking approach he had not originally planned.

The Spaniard also turned up with a moustache, the result of a team bet that everyone would grow one if he won Tokyo. Bergs, who thrashed Ignacio Buse 6-0, 6-3, is next, with a possible fourth-round clash against defending champion Valentin Vacherot. Daniil Medvedev and Felix Auger-Aliassime both came from a set down to advance.

sports.h3: Van de Zandschulp knocks out Michelsen in Shanghai
sports.summary: Botic van de Zandschulp beat 31st seed Alex Michelsen 6-4, 6-4 as defending champion Valentin Vacherot also moved through.
body: Dutch number one Botic van de Zandschulp produced one of the cleaner upsets of the second round, beating American Alex Michelsen 6-4, 6-4 to reach the last 32 of the Masters 1000 event.

Vacherot, who won the title last year as world number 204, opened his defence with a 6-4, 7-6(5) win over Sebastian Baez and meets Tommy Paul next. Stefanos Tsitsipas reached 400 tour-level wins against Luciano Darderi, while Taylor Fritz, Casper Ruud and Arthur Fils also progressed.

sports.h3: World No. 277 Zhou Yi stuns Musetti
sports.summary: Chinese wild card Zhou Yi saved three set points to beat Lorenzo Musetti in two tiebreaks and now faces Djokovic's conqueror Hubert Hurkacz.
body: Home wild card Zhou Yi pulled off the biggest upset of the opening days in Shanghai, beating former world number five Lorenzo Musetti 7-6(7), 3-6, 7-6(1). Zhou saved three set points in the opener and dominated the deciding tiebreak.

His reward is a third-round match against Hubert Hurkacz, who ended Novak Djokovic's run on Friday. Top seed Alexander Zverev survived an ankle scare against Wu Yibing and meets Quentin Halys, while Flavio Cobolli and Andrey Rublev were among the seeds to fall early.

sports.h3: Hurricane cuts J/22 Worlds short in New Orleans
sports.summary: Glenn Darden won the 46-boat J/22 World Championship after racing was halted following day two as Hurricane Isaias closed in on the Gulf coast.
body: The J/22 World Championship in New Orleans was scheduled for 7 to 10 October but organisers stopped racing after two days and seven races as Hurricane Isaias approached. Forecasts had the storm reaching Category 2 strength with winds near 110 mph at landfall.
American Glenn Darden was declared champion after dominating the shortened series. The event became one of several on the US calendar disrupted by an active late hurricane season.

sports.h3: Route du Rhum village opens in nine days
sports.summary: A record-sized 118-boat fleet across six classes is due to leave Saint-Malo for Guadeloupe on 1 November, with the race village opening on 20 October.
body: Saint-Malo is preparing for the 2026 Route du Rhum, which starts on Sunday 1 November at 13:02. A total of 118 solo skippers are entered across the Ultim, Ocean Fifty, IMOCA and Class40 fleets plus two new vintage categories for multihulls and monohulls.

The race village opens on 20 October around the Vauban and Duguay-Trouin basins and runs for almost two weeks. Charles Caudrelier defends his Ultim title against Armel Le Cleac'h, Thomas Coville, Tom Laperche and Anthony Marchand.

sports.h3: Feyenoord beat AZ to end their unbeaten start
sports.summary: Goals from Nacho Ferri and Javi Lopez gave Feyenoord a 2-0 win over leaders AZ in De Kuip, lifting the Rotterdam side to the top of the Eredivisie.
body: Feyenoord handed AZ their first league defeat of the season on Saturday evening. Nacho Ferri opened the scoring after 13 minutes and Javi Lopez doubled the lead just before the hour as Danny Makkelie's match stayed firmly in Feyenoord's control.

AZ arrived top with 19 points from seven games, two clear of Feyenoord. The result flips the order after matchday eight and keeps the title race tight with PSV, who won at home to Heerenveen on Friday.

sports.h3: Ajax held by NEC again in Amsterdam
sports.summary: Tolu Arokodare's early goal was cancelled out by a Tjaronn Chery penalty as Ajax drew 1-1 with NEC for the second season running.
body: Ajax started brightly at the Johan Cruijff ArenA when Tolu Arokodare scored in the seventh minute, but Tjaronn Chery levelled from the spot 12 minutes later and the hosts could not find a winner.
The draw leaves Ajax fifth on 15 points after eight matches, already well off the pace set by Feyenoord, AZ and PSV. NEC extended their unbeaten record in Amsterdam to four seasons.

sports.h3: FloGrappling boss says UFC BJJ is losing money
sports.summary: Ben Kovacs argues the economics of pro grappling rarely work and that the UFC's jiu-jitsu events cannot be profitable at current pay and production costs.
body: FloGrappling general manager Ben Kovacs used a podcast appearance to argue that most fans only care about a handful of high-stakes matchups, so events should be shorter. He held up Fight to Win as one of the few promotions that works, thanks to tight venue costs, athletes who help sell tickets and modest prize money.

Kovacs said he knows what UFC BJJ pays and what production costs, and is certain the promotion is losing money. He estimated that 10,000 subscribers at five dollars would cover only about a third of a main event purse, and blamed inflated athlete expectations partly on old star contracts.

sports.h3: Victor Hugo explains his ADCC retirement
sports.summary: The heavyweight submitted all four opponents at ADCC 2026, then skipped the absolute and walked away from the event, though a 2028 return in Brazil is not ruled out.
body: Victor Hugo said a pre-event question from Ben Kovacs about retiring if he won everything planted the idea. As the submissions piled up in the +99 kg division, he decided to set the standard and leave on a high.

He skipped the absolute because of the long wait between the finals and the open bracket and doubts about his recovery. When reminded that ADCC 2028 is rumoured for Brazil, Hugo admitted that prospect was exciting.

sports.h3: Zuchi stripped of IBJJF world title over doping
sports.summary: Rider Zuchi has been banned for three years and lost his 2026 heavyweight world title after testing positive for anabolic steroids.
body: A sample taken from Rider Zuchi at the IBJJF World Championship on 31 May showed drostanolone and a nandrolone metabolite. USADA announced the sanction and the IBJJF has revised the results.

Nicholas Maglicic, beaten by Zuchi in the final, becomes the official heavyweight world champion. Zuchi received a one-year reduction for admitting the violation and is eligible again from 1 July 2027.

sports.h3: Tasoev ends Kokauri's home dream in Baku final
sports.summary: Inal Tasoev retained the +100 kg world title against Azerbaijan's Ushangi Kokauri, while 19-year-old Lee Hyeonji won the women's +78 kg crown.
body: The final individual day of the World Championships in Baku ended in disappointment for the home crowd as Inal Tasoev beat Ushangi Kokauri in the heavyweight final, leaving Kokauri with silver once again. Lukas Krpalek and Azerbaijan's Kanan Nasibov took bronze, and Dutchman Jur Spijkers finished seventh.

South Korean teenager Lee Hyeonji needed less than five minutes of total fight time to dominate the women's heavyweight category, beating France's Romane Dicko in the final. The championships close today with the mixed team event.

consumer-tech.h3: PC shipments plunge 20% as memory crunch bites
consumer-tech.summary: IDC counted 62.7 million PCs shipped in Q3 2026, down 20.1% on a year earlier, and warned high prices will persist.
body: Global PC shipments fell to 62.7 million units in the third quarter, according to IDC. That is 9.1 percent below the previous quarter and 20.1 percent below the same period in 2025, as the AI-driven memory shortage keeps pushing up component costs.

IDC blamed supply problems and elevated prices for suppressing demand. Its consumer devices research director said retailers now fear carrying too much stock, which could bring some promotions, but prices will stay far above last year's levels and the outlook could worsen before it improves.
The figures follow IDC's first quarterly decline in nine quarters back in July and repeated cuts to its 2026 forecast. Buyers who can wait are being advised to hold off for a year if possible.

consumer-tech.h3: Intel revives old socket to keep DDR4 alive
consumer-tech.summary: Gigabyte says Intel will launch new CPUs on the five-year-old LGA 1700 socket in early 2027, likely so buyers can stick with much cheaper DDR4 memory.
body: Motherboard maker Gigabyte has indicated that Intel plans fresh processors for LGA 1700, a socket introduced in 2021. The expectation is refreshed Raptor Lake and Alder Lake chips that can run on DDR4.

The logic is cost. A 32GB DDR4 kit sells for around $210 while an equivalent DDR5 kit costs upwards of $480. Intel has not confirmed the plan, but a company vice president recently said Raptor Lake will stay around for years partly because demand for DDR4 platforms remains strong.

consumer-tech.h3: Next Google TV Streamer gets mics and presence sensing
consumer-tech.summary: A slimmer second-generation Google TV Streamer is in development with built-in microphones, a faster chip, more storage and a revised remote.
body: 9to5Google reports that Google is working on a new TV Streamer that keeps the current shape but is narrower. Cutouts on the slanted top will house microphones for hands-free Hey Google commands.

It also adds presence sensing to wake an ambient screen when someone enters the room, plus a faster processor and more than the current 32GB of storage. The remote gains two extra shortcut buttons. No launch date is known, and the refresh follows a $50 price rise for the existing model in August.

consumer-tech.h3: Panos Panay teases more Alexa hardware and 'Neo'
consumer-tech.summary: Amazon's devices chief hinted that more Alexa-branded products are coming and let slip a new cross-device design language called Neo.
body: Speaking at the launch of the Alexa Tablet series, which replaces the Fire tablets, Panos Panay confirmed it is the first Amazon hardware branded Alexa. Asked whether more would follow, he said not that reporters had seen yet.

He also revealed that design lead Ralf Groene is building a Neo design language meant to tie AI conversations together across devices so users can pick up where they left off. Panay promised more on Neo and new Echo hardware later this month.

consumer-tech.h3: Free Gemini users now limited to Flash-Lite
consumer-tech.summary: Since 9 October, people using the Gemini app without a paid plan can only pick the Flash-Lite model, while AI Plus subscribers lose Pro.
body: Google has tightened model access in the Gemini app. Personal accounts without a subscription now only get Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite, losing both Flash and Pro, while the $4.99 AI Plus tier keeps Flash but drops Pro on a cutoff date Google is emailing to each account.

Reports initially said AI Pro would gain Deep Think, but Google's help pages have been inconsistent on that point. All models are also getting low, medium and high effort settings this month, with higher effort consuming more of a user's limits.

consumer-tech.h3: iOS 27.2 with new Siri languages due late October
consumer-tech.summary: Siri AI support for French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish arrives in iOS 27.2, likely in the week of 26 October, but not for iPhones in the EU.
body: Apple is testing iOS 27.2 unusually early because iOS 27.1 is reserved for the iPhone Duo, which launches on 23 October. The second public beta landed on 6 October.

Apple has promised the five new Siri AI languages in October, which effectively confirms the release month. The update also brings Apple TV app profiles, Dual Capture for Group FaceTime and a reworked Up Next in Podcasts. Siri AI remains unavailable on iPhones and iPads in the EU.

consumer-tech.h3: Pixel Watch 4 gets Gemini watch face generator
consumer-tech.summary: A rolling update brings the Pixel Watch 5's AI watch face creator and its stock faces to last year's model.
body: Pixel Watch 4 owners are reporting an update that adds the text-prompt watch face generator introduced with the Pixel Watch 5. Users describe the look they want in the Pixel Watch app and Gemini builds a matching design.

The update also brings the newer model's Weave, Modular, Reveal and Chronograph faces plus a Steph Curry dial. Separately, Google Health 5.10 is rolling out with irregular rhythm notifications in Japan.

consumer-tech.h3: Emmys move to Prime Video from 2027
consumer-tech.summary: Amazon has won exclusive global rights to stream the Emmy Awards free in more than 240 countries and territories under a six-year deal.
body: The deal with the Television Academy ends the long rotation of the ceremony between ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC. Viewers will not need a Prime subscription to watch, and Amazon is reportedly paying $20 million to $25 million a year.
The Emmys become the first major entertainment awards show to go streaming-only, ahead of the Oscars' move to YouTube in 2029.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla Model 3 and Model Y can now power homes
consumer-tech.summary: Powershare home backup now works on new Model 3 and Model Y cars in the US when paired with a Powerwall 3.
body: Tesla has extended Powershare vehicle-to-home backup to its best-selling cars. Model 3 and Model Y vehicles ordered from 1 October are supported, along with some earlier cars, and owners can check under Additional Vehicle Info in the software menu.
A Powerwall 3 is required for now and the system delivers up to 11.52 kW, with Tesla claiming more than two days of backup for a typical home. Feeding power back to the grid is not supported.

consumer-tech.h3: BYD opens orders for bigger 'Great Seagull'
consumer-tech.summary: Blind pre-orders are open in China for the second-generation Seagull, which grows by 425 mm and switches to a 95 kW rear motor.
body: BYD's cheapest EV, sold abroad as the Dolphin Surf, is getting much larger. Regulatory filings show the new model at 4,205 mm long with a 2,650 mm wheelbase, a 95 kW rear motor in place of the old 55 kW front unit and a roof-mounted lidar.
Prices have not been announced. The current car starts at about 69,900 yuan and was the world's sixth best-selling EV through August. A full launch is expected before the end of 2026.

consumer-tech.h3: Hyundai cuts Ioniq 5 and Ioniq 9 prices by 10%
consumer-tech.summary: Ahead of 2027 models, Hyundai is taking $3,500 off the Ioniq 5 and up to $7,000 off the three-row Ioniq 9 in the US this month.
body: The 2026 Ioniq 5, already one of the cheapest EVs in the US from about $35,000, is $3,500 off in October, with leases from $339 a month. The Ioniq 9 gets up to $7,000 in savings from a $58,995 base price.
Hyundai is also offering low-rate financing on both models. The deals arrive as the US EV market adjusts to life without the federal tax credit, which ended a year ago.

consumer-tech.h3: Tesla opens first Semi Megachargers in Georgia
consumer-tech.summary: Two sites near Atlanta and Savannah with 14 stalls rated up to 1.2 MW create the Tesla Semi's first public corridor outside California.
body: Tesla has switched on an eight-stall Megacharger site in Conley south of Atlanta and a six-stall site at a Pilot truck stop in Ellabell near the Port of Savannah. The two are about 220 miles apart, letting even the standard-range Semi run the busy port-to-Atlanta freight lane.

The Pilot site is the first from a partnership announced in January, a season later than planned. Tesla is well behind its target of roughly 37 Megacharger sites this year, even as Semi volume production starts in Nevada.

consumer-tech.summary: Jaguar unveiled its four-door Type 01 in New York, a high-performance electric GT expected to start around 120,000 pounds in the UK.
body: The Type 01 is the first production car of Jaguar's all-electric relaunch and was revealed in New York this week. UK pricing is expected from about 120,000 pounds, with heavily personalised cars going well beyond 150,000.
Orders are due to open in early 2027 and first deliveries are planned for the second half of that year. Australian reports put local pricing near 300,000 Australian dollars.
